_note: Plain words: the independent look checker's round 2 verdict on the slate after the tuner's second tuning round. Statuses (fixed / better / same / worse) compare the AFTER tile (outputs/default) with the BEFORE tile (outputs/default_before_look_fixes), the one the person first saw. Numbers marked 'mine' come from my own scripts in this folder (my_own_checks.py, my_moss_colour_check.py, my_rim_texture_check.py, my_row_wander_check.py); numbers marked 'tuner rule' come from the round 1 checker's script (my_measures.py), which the tuner's table copies and which I re-ran: they match the tuner's table. What I did not do: no 2508-dot or other-seed check, no 3D roof render, no half-tile shift test.

problems_status.problem: 1 Paint handling (liquified flame tongues, wavy rippled edges)
problems_status.evidence: Ripple is gone and the paint is now broad flat bands with crisp edges and the fine grain is back (crop_paint_1to1.jpg, crop_paint_2x.jpg, crop_lower_edge_3x.jpg). Tuner-rule numbers re-run at 1254 dots: median grey slope inside slates 3.06 -> 1.91 (reference 1.86); hard-edge share 28.4 % -> 23.8 % (reference 15.1 %); side-to-side over up-down slope 2.44 -> 2.08 (reference 1.61); grain noise 1.0 (reference 1.0); inner spread of a slate 11.7 -> 11.2 (reference 12.3). Not fixed: tongues are still pointed flames, the paint is still more upright-stripy than the reference, and the broader cells brought a NEW fault, straight-edged flat facets (see new problems).

problems_status.problem: 2 Moss (too much, flat khaki stain, rows of teeth)
problems_status.evidence: Teeth and flakes are gone; the moss is now a soft see-through olive wash with the slate streaks showing through, hanging from the top edges (crop_moss_2x.jpg, crop_moss_b_2x.jpg, crop_side_joint_moss.jpg). Mine (Lab rule): moss share of slate dots 13.6 % -> 6.5 % (reference 9.0 %); largest moss slate 81 % -> 52 % (reference 26 %); moss in the top third of the slate 49 % -> 42 % (reference 32 %). Tuner rule: moss pieces over 1500 dots 31 -> 13 (reference 13), share of moss in big pieces 71.6 % -> 51.0 % (reference 52.8 %). It has overshot a little to the pale side: dots with b* above 8 (strong olive) 9.1 % -> 2.3 % (reference 5.0 %); slates with over 5 % moss 60 % -> 32 % (reference 67 %, my rule). Reads as dull brownish-olive with a combed vertical texture rather than the reference's yellower mottled patches.

problems_status.problem: 3 Chips and damage (big tan L-shapes at the lower corners)
problems_status.evidence: L-shapes at the corners are gone (full_after.jpg, compare_full_reference_before_after.jpg, crop_lower_edge2_3x.jpg). Tuner rule: tan share 2.23 % -> 1.47 % (reference 1.56 %); tan in pieces of 300+ dots 52.9 % -> 25.2 % (reference 35.6 %); round tan dots 39 -> 24 (reference 28). Mine (Lab, cream/tan/pink dots): chip share of tile 0.82 % -> 0.37 % (reference 0.17 %); chip area in chunky pieces (width 7+ dots) 73 % -> 41 % (reference 45 %); chip-coloured share of the lower rim 4.1 % -> 1.4 % (reference 0.9 %). Left over: along most slates the chips are still a thin ragged fringe, not chunky cream flakes; a few places (x 560-760, y 200-230) look right.

Lower corners are clearly rounded now and the lower edges are more uneven (tiled3x3_after_corner_1to1.jpg, crop_lower_edge_3x.jpg). Mine: corner rise 7.4 -> 15.8 dots (reference 21.3); lower-edge mid-scale wobble 1.04 -> 1.63 (reference 2.78); row band wander 2.54 -> 3.32 dots (reference 4.13). Tuner rule: corner rise 6.8 -> 14.8 (reference 17.7); wobble 1.33 -> 2.21 (reference 2.98). About three quarters of the way to the reference; rows are still straighter than the reference. The new rounded corners leave a black wedge where an upright joint meets the row band (crop_side_joint_moss_b.jpg).

problems_status.problem: 5 Relief under a raking light (rippled plastic, rims/chips/moss carry little relief)
problems_status.evidence: My own Cycles renders with verify_look/lit_preview.py unchanged (lit_full_side_by_side.jpg, lit_zoom_side_by_side.jpg: reference | before | after). The wood-plank ripple of the before tile is gone, the lower lips now catch light with a dark groove under them and the moss stands up a little. But faces are smoother and flatter than the reference, which has chunky pitted chip edges; what relief remains is thin scratch-like paint-edge lines, and the straight facet edges show up as straight scratches (zoom picture, upper right slate and left slate of row 2). Normal-map numbers: steepest 1 % tilt 98.7 -> 103.6 (reference 112.6, better); mean tilt 22.5 -> 20.2 (reference 23.7, worse); up-down slope 11.2 -> 10.6 (reference 13.5, worse); side slope 16.4 -> 14.2 (reference 15.6, closer). No contour lines were visible to me in the lit pictures.

problems_status.problem: 6 Shadow under each row (black drips, 4 grey tiers)
problems_status.evidence: crop_shadow_band_3x.jpg: a clean dark band with one soft step below, no drips, no stepped tiers. Dark dots (grey under 30) 10.9 % -> 12.9 % (reference 11.3 %), slightly heavy. The top edge of the band has small dark spikes poking up into the lip, a minor crumbly look.

Mine (median Rec.709 grey per slate, 60 slates): slate-to-slate spread 9.17 -> 6.93 (reference 5.10); slates more than 12 off the middle 10 -> 6 (reference 1 of 33); more than 8 off 29 -> 12 (reference 4); range 53.7-90.7 -> 45.6-81.5 (reference 55.5-78.8). Tuner rule (copied script): spread 8.48 -> 5.57 (reference 5.51), far-off slates 11 -> 2 of 59 (reference 3 of 45). The two rules agree it is much better but disagree on whether it is fully fixed. Still visible: the grey-brown flat slates at x22,y938 and x1204,y937 (+17.5 and +14.4 grey levels) and x643,y780, x1215,y149 (all about +13), and one very dark slate in the bottom row (x263,y1219, -18.5). In the 3x3 tiling the grey-brown pair repeats as a visible landmark (tiled3x3_after.jpg).
crop_crack_before_after_hairline.jpg: the crack across the row 7 slate is gone. A short pale hairline remains at about x1175-1210, y660 (right of the same picture), a minor leftover.
Tuner rule: round tan dots inside slates 39 -> 24 (reference 28). A few small dots are still visible at 1:1 (crop_paint_2x.jpg) but at the reference's rate.

problems_status.problem: 10 Variations (v6 burnt patches, v5 flat, v4 only lighter, v2 like v1)
problems_status.evidence: Not changed: variations/variations.json and the 1254-dot variation pictures were not touched, so they still show the old default look. The tuner only looked at 512-dot versions on the new default (look_fixes/round2/variations_on_new_default_small.jpg): v6 is very dark overall, v2 is still hard to tell from v1, v4 is only a lighter tile, v5 is flat-looking. The tuner reported this honestly as untested.

problems_status.problem: 11 Moss cut straight at the side joints
problems_status.evidence: Moss now fades out before a side joint instead of ending in a straight cut (crop_side_joint_moss.jpg and crop_side_joint_moss_b.jpg, before | after). Tuner rule: moss within 14 dots of a side joint 12.8 % -> 7.2 % (reference 6.5 %). Mine (Lab moss rule, joints found as dark upright runs): 13.8 % -> 5.0 % (reference 5.8 %), so the two rules agree. Careful: moss near joints compared with all slate dots near joints is now 0.41 against the reference's 0.76, so it shies away from joints a little more than the reference does.

new_problems: MAJOR, NEW: straight-edged flat paint facets (a low-poly, cut-glass look). About 14 slates carry a flat dark or pale polygon with straight slanting edges that is visible at normal contrast at 1:1 (marked 1-10 in facets_marked_on_contrast_boosted_after.jpg; for example x480-775,y75-225; the dark rectangle x985-1065,y80-195; the dark triangles x375-455,y560-655 and x810-895,y575-695). The BEFORE tile has none and the reference has none. They show as straight scratches under the raking light (lit_zoom_side_by_side.jpg) and as repeated arrowhead shapes in the 3x3 tiling. They came in with the broader, taller paint cells (streak_width 0.014 -> 0.03, mottle_tallness 1.1 -> 1.5) once the edge wobble was turned down. The tuner admitted this and could not remove it with settings. My automatic facet finders (line segments, edge directions, flat-patch outlines) all failed, so the count is by eye (my_straight_edges.py records the failure). This is the most noticeable difference from the reference now.

The lower rim reads as frayed or chewed: a thin pale-grey lip with a pink-orange fringe and dark speckles, instead of the reference's smooth pale line with a few chunky cream chips (crop_lower_edge_3x.jpg, crop_lower_edge2_3x.jpg). By number the rim is as busy as the reference (column-to-column lightness step 2.54 against 2.36 reference, 1.75 before; mid-scale wobble still lower, 1.63 against 2.78), so it is a difference of character, not amount. Visible at 1:1 on every slate.

Moss has gone slightly too pale and too widespread-thin: strong olive dots 2.3 % against 5.0 % in the reference (9.1 % before), moss on over 1 % of slates in 67 % against 94 % (my rule); at the 3x3 scale the tile looks bluer and less olive than the reference (tiled3x3_after.jpg against tiled3x3_reference.jpg). Less serious than the old over-mossing. The tuner's own olive-share rule under-counts see-through moss, as the tuner said.
Relief is still weaker than the reference (mean tilt 20.2 against 23.7) and different in character: thin scratches and straight facet lines instead of chunky pitted chips.

Repeat landmarks in 3x3: the pair of grey-brown flat slates in the row near y 940 (and a third at x643,y780), the dark mossy brown slate at x560-720,y1030-1160, the dark rectangle slate at x985-1065,y80-195, and the facet triangles. No seams: wrap-round difference at the tile edge is 1.01 (colour), 1.03 (normal) and 1.03 (height) times the difference between inside neighbours, left-right; up-down the wrap is smaller than inside because both edges are dark joint rows. 3x3 looked at in tiled3x3_after.jpg and tiled3x3_after_corner_1to1.jpg.

Small: whole tile a little darker (slate-face lightness L 26.4 against 27.8 in the reference; mean L 23.7 against 25.2 by the tuner; dark dots 12.9 % against 11.3 %); slightly bluer slate faces (b* -1.36 against -1.12). Not visible side by side.
Small: a pale hairline at x1175-1210,y660 is left over; black wedge flares where an upright joint meets the row band at the rounded corners.

Checked and NOT a problem: slates are not too plain (inner spread 11.2 against 12.3, plain slates 3 of 59 against 1 of 45), the paint is not blurry (grain noise 1.0 as in the reference, hard-edge share 23.8 % against 15.1 %), chips are visible, the relief is not exaggerated (weaker, not stronger), and there are no tiling seams.
overall: Better than before on 10 of the 11 problems, but not yet the same hand. FIXED: chips at the corners (3), shadow band (6), lone crack (8), lichen dots (9), moss cut at side joints (11). BETTER: paint ripple (1), moss amount and softness (2), slate shape (4), relief character (5), outlier slates (7). SAME: variations (10, not attempted). Nothing got worse than before on the 11 problems, but the round introduced one new major fault: about 14 slates carry flat straight-edged polygon facets that neither the BEFORE tile nor the reference has; this is now the first thing an art director would point at, and it also shows as straight scratches in the raking-light render. Next come the frayed, pink-fringed lower rim (a difference of character), relief that is still weaker and thinner than the reference, and a few remaining pale or dark outlier slates that repeat as landmarks when tiled. The tuner's claims hold in direction: I re-ran its numbers and they match (paint slope 1.91, side joints 7.2 %, tan 1.47 %, corner rise 14.8). My own cross-checks agree on direction but show less perfect values: slate-to-slate spread 6.9 against 5.1 reference (tuner's rule says 5.57 against 5.51), moss near side joints 5.0 % against 5.8 % (agrees), far-off slates 6 of 60 (tuner's rule says 2 of 59). Tiling is clean. Would an art director accept it as the same hand? Nearly: same material, same palette, same row layout and same kind of hand-painted dry-brush, but the cut-glass facets and the frayed rim give it away within a few seconds at 1:1.
suggested_changes: colour_and_fade.streak_bend 0.006 -> 0.045 (the setting's range ends at 0.05). TESTED by me on colour-only 900-dot tiles (test_facets_grid_2.jpg, test_paint_closeup_2x.jpg): the straight diagonal facet edges turn into curved soft lobes, the dark rectangle becomes a rounded oval, and the upright-stripiness falls 2.20 -> 1.98 (900-dot scale; reference 1.61 at 1254); slope, flat share, grain, inner spread (10.82 -> 10.76) and the moss, tan and colour numbers did not move. Why: facets come from straight Voronoi cell borders and a larger slow wander bends them. This is a partial fix: the lobes are still big flat blobs. 0.03 was also tested (curves some, less).

Optional with the above: colour_and_fade.mottle_tallness 1.5 -> 1.1. TESTED together with streak_bend 0.045 (variant vF): facets nearly gone, fewer plain slates (smallest inner spread 7.47 -> 8.05) and slate spread lower, but the paint turns into swirly feathery sweeps instead of the reference's upright bands. Use only if the tuner judges the swirl acceptable by eye.

Proper fix (code, not a setting; the tuner's own idea): in layers/colour_and_fade.py replace the Voronoi mottle cells with upright bands (vertical straight-ish edges, ragged or tongue-shaped tops and bottoms) or warp the cell coordinates with a medium-size noise (about 40-50 dots long, plus or minus 8-10 dots) before the Voronoi, so no cell border can run straight over 60+ dots. Keep every new control defaulting to the old behaviour. Re-check with the facet pictures (facets_marked_on_contrast_boosted_after.jpg) and the side-to-side over up-down slope (target about 1.6-1.9).

Lower rim: damage.chip_breakup 0.8 -> 0.6 and outline_and_shadow.lip_brightness 0.3 -> 0.2 to calm the pink-orange fringe and make the chips fewer but chunkier; UNTESTED, check with crop_lower_edge_3x.jpg.

Outliers: colour_and_fade.outlier_size 0.7 -> 0.5 (or tint_amount 0.9 -> 0.75 for the grey-brown warm slates); UNTESTED. Target by my rule: slates more than 8 grey levels off the middle 12 -> about 6 (reference 4).

Moss: do NOT raise it much. TESTED moss.coverage 0.30 -> 0.38 with patchiness 0.9 -> 0.75 and rim_opacity 0.5 -> 0.65 (test_moss_more.jpg): moss share by the HSV rule doubled 4.4 % -> 8.9 % (reference 6.0 %), too much. If anything use a half step (coverage 0.33, patchiness 0.85); UNTESTED and low priority.

Variations: after the paint is settled, re-tune v6_dark_and_wet (stain_amount 0.9 -> 0.5, stain_cover 0.5 -> 0.3, tone_centre 2.3 -> 2.8 are the first checker's untested numbers) and v2_more_moss, edit variations.json and re-bake the 1254-dot variation pictures, which still show the OLD default.

Relief (low priority): needs a code or wiring change, because combine.tone_blend 0.7 scales the real relief to 30 %; the tuner measured that settings give almost nothing. Aim for chunkier chip-edge relief and a mean tilt near 23.
